patch.summary:
Thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Salesforce documents a broader use-case set; Keap is narrower/specialist.

Frame: General-purpose vs specialist — Salesforce documents a broader use-case set; Keap is narrower/specialist.. Choose Keap only if use-case priority is lead-management and Salesforce is secondary for that motion. Choose Salesforce only if your buying job matches “Enterprise CRM platform for sales, service, marketing, and customer data across large and ” rather than Keap's shape. Workflow advantage: Keap leans email-outreach; Salesforce leans pipeline-management, account-management. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Salesforce documents a broader use-case set; Keap is narrower/specialist.
- Workflow coverage skew: Keap-leaning email-outreach vs Salesforce-leaning pipeline-management, account-management, complex-sales-processes.
- Researched limits: Keap — Base plans start at $249/mo annually for two users; additional users are $39/mo each.; Salesforce — USD list pricing rises quickly: Pro Suite $100, Enterprise $175, Unlimited $350 per user/month (annual). Add-ons (Agentforce for Sales from $125 Contact us, Revenue Intelligence, Success Plans) increase TCO..

Limitations — Keap: Base plans start at $249/mo annually for two users; additional users are $39/mo each.; Contact capacity and voice/SMS allotments scale by Max tier; overages apply for texts/voice minutes.; Salesforce: USD list pricing rises quickly: Pro Suite $100, Enterprise $175, Unlimited $350 per user/month (annual). Add-ons (Agentforce for Sales from $125 Contact us, Revenue Intelligence, Success Plans) increase TCO.; Premier Support is an add-on on Pro Suite. Agentforce for Sales, Sales Programs, Revenue Intelligence, and Revenue Cloud are separate paid add-ons; some require Contact us..

Poor-fit cases: Keap is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Base plans start at $249/mo annually for two users; additional users are $39/mo each. · Salesforce is a poor fit when that limitation bites: USD list pricing rises quickly: Pro Suite $100, Enterprise $175, Unlimited $350 per user/month (annual). Add-ons (Agentforce for Sales from $125 Contact us, Revenue Intelligence, Success Plans) increase TCO.

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
